extracted.intended_audience: examiners and staff of International Preliminary Examining Authorities (IPEAs) and national/intergovernmental patent office examiners handling PCT international preliminary examination
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive guidance for conducting international preliminary examination under the PCT (starting conditions, required documents, language/translation rules, search practice, unity, written opinions and report timing). Targeted to examiners and IPEA administrative staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement concerning amendments (Box No. IV, part 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The first part of Box No. IV of the demand Form provides check boxes for the applicant to indicate the basis on which international preliminary examination should start. Where none of the boxes are marked or where the applicant has indicated that the international preliminary examination is to start on the basis of the international application as originally filed, the file is forwarded to the examiner as soon as all formal (including any required translation of the international application and/or of amendments) and fee matters are resolved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If boxes are not marked or applicant elects original-filed basis, forward file once formalities and fees resolved. Marking the check boxes controls whether IPEA waits for amendments (see separate criteria for Article 19/34).

rubrics_metrics.name: Taking into account amendments under Article 34
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the international preliminary examination is to take into account amendments under Article 34, but the applicant failed to submit them with the demand, the IPEA invites the applicant (Form PCT/IPEA/431) within a reasonable time limit fixed in the invitation to submit the amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether submitted with the demand or later, amendments are to be marked in accordance with Section 602(a)(i) to (iii) and (b) of the Administrative Instructions before the file is forwarded to the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taking into account amendments under Article 19
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant marked the appropriate check box that Article 19 amendments (and accompanying statement) are to be taken into account, the IPEA indicates on the last sheet of the demand whether a copy was submitted with the demand. Where no copy was submitted, examination does not start until a copy of such amendment and any accompanying statement are received from the International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The International Bureau promptly transmits any Article 19 amendments and required letters; the IPEA marks amendments per Section 602 before forwarding to the examiner. The IPEA may opt to receive 'no amendment received' notifications electronically rather than by mail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postponement where ISA = IPEA and applicant requested postponement (Rule 53.9(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the same national Office or intergovernmental organization acts as both ISA and IPEA and wishes to start preliminary examination at the same time as the search but the demand includes a statement postponing the start under Rule 53.9(b), the IPEA waits until it receives copies of any Article 19 amendments or a notice from the applicant that no Article 19 amendments will be made before beginning the examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If neither copy nor notice is received by the expiration of the Article 19 filing time limit (16 months from priority date or two months from transmittal of ISR, whichever is later), examination starts on the basis of documents in the file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language for the purposes of international preliminary examination (Box No. IV, part 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The second part of Box No. IV allows the applicant to indicate the language in which international preliminary examination is to be carried out: (i) language of filing; (ii) language of a translation furnished for the international search; (iii) language of publication; or (iv) language of a translation furnished for international preliminary examination (subject to acceptance by the Authority and being a language of publication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If none marked, forward the file once the language is determined and any required translations furnished. Translations used must include elements referred to in Article 11(1)(iii)(d)/(e) and any parts considered to have been contained in the international application under Rule 20.6(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation to furnish missing translation or accompanying letter (language-related defects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the international preliminary examination is to be carried out on a translation but the applicant failed to submit it with the demand, the IPEA invites the applicant (Form PCT/IPEA/443) to submit the missing items within a reasonable time limit. The same applies where a letter required under Rule 66.8(a) or Rule 46.5(b) is not provided in the language of the translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the translation filed under Rule 55.2(a) does not meet the physical requirements of Rule 11, the IPEA may invite correction. Failure to comply with an invitation to furnish a translation of an amendment means the amendment shall not be taken into account during international preliminary examination; failure to furnish an accompanying letter means the amendment need not be taken into account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents to be present in the IPEA file
rubrics_metrics.description: When the IPEA is part of the same national Office/intergovernmental organization as the ISA, the file should include: the demand; description, drawings (if any), claims as originally filed; the abstract as filed or established by the ISA (or translations if necessary); any amendments proposed to date or notification none filed; the ISR with applicant's comments and copies of cited documents; the written opinion of the ISA; and, as appropriate, requests and correspondence, the priority document and any required translations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all documents and translations are present/marked per Administrative Instructions before forwarding to examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of translation transmitted to ISA where ISA = IPEA
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a translation is required under Rule 55.2 and the ISA and IPEA are part of the same national Office/organization, the IPEA carries out the international preliminary examination on the basis of any translation transmitted to the ISA under Rule 23.1(b) unless the applicant furnishes a further translation for the purposes of the international preliminary examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPEA may accept the translation already provided to ISA unless a different translation is submitted specifically for IPE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply of file elements where ISA ≠ IPEA
rubrics_metrics.description: When the ISA and IPEA are not the same, elements are supplied as follows: demand by applicant; request/description/drawings/claims by the International Bureau; ISR or Article 17(2)(a) declaration and written opinion by the International Bureau; translations required under Rule 55.2 by the applicant (subject to paragraph 18.11 exception); Article 19 amendments by IB transmission or applicant; sequence listings by ISA if same-office IPEA else by applicant; Article 34(2)(b) amendments by applicant; copies of documents cited in ISR not available in IPEA databases by the ISA; priority document by IB; translation of priority document by applicant (subject to invitation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the listed allocation of responsibility to ensure the IPEA receives all necessary material for examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appraising an Article 17(2)(a) declaration as if it were an international search report
rubrics_metrics.description: If the file contains a declaration under Article 17(2)(a) (ISA declares it considered the application not required to be searched or that a meaningful search could not be carried out), the examiner should appraise the declaration as if it were the international search report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the declaration substantively like an ISR for purposes of preliminary examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective of international preliminary examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective is to formulate a preliminary and non-binding opinion as to: (i) whether the claimed invention appears to be novel; (ii) whether the claimed invention appears to involve an inventive step (non-obvious); and (iii) whether the claimed invention appears to be industrially applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These three criteria are the basis of international preliminary examination; see Chapters 12–14 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit substantive criteria: sufficiency of disclosure and technical character
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability, the examiner should be aware the invention must be such that it can be carried out by a person skilled in the art (Article 5) and must relate to a technical field, be concerned with a technical problem and have technical features definable in the claim (Rule 5.1(a)(i), 5.1(a)(iii), 6.3(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These requirements are implicitly contained in the Treaty and Regulations and relevant to evaluating inventive step and industrial applicability; advantageous effects may be relevant when determining inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for the start of international preliminary examination (Rule 69.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPEA normally starts preliminary examination when it is in possession of: (i) the demand; (ii) the full handling fee and preliminary examination fee (including late fee if applicable); (iii) required translation under Rule 55.2; and (iv) either the ISR or the Article 17(2)(a) declaration, and the written opinion established under Rule 43bis.1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any of these are missing, the IPEA should not start until they are available, subject to the exceptions laid out in paragraph 19.08.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions delaying start of examination (Article 34/Article 19/34 and postponement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exceptions include: (a) statement that Article 19 amendments are to be taken into account — IPEA waits for copy of amendments; (b) statement that Article 34 amendments submitted with the demand but not actually submitted — IPEA waits for amendments or expiry of invitation time limit; (c) where ISA also acts as IPEA and wishes concurrent start, the IPEA may start with search unless applicant indicated postponement until after Article 19 time limit; (d) if applicant indicated postponement until expiration of time limit for making a demand, IPEA waits until that time limit expires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specific subparagraph rules (19.08 (a)-(d)) to determine when examination should commence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary international search reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Any supplementary international search reports transmitted to the Authority in sufficient time should be taken into account for the purpose of a written opinion or international preliminary examination report as if they were part of the main ISR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplementary ISRs received after the Authority has started to draw up an opinion or report need not be taken into account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for establishment of the international preliminary examination report (Rule 69.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The time limit for establishment of the international preliminary examination report may not exceed whichever expires last of: (i) 28 months from the priority date; (ii) six months from the time period provided under Rule 69.1 for the start of the international preliminary examination; or (iii) six months from the date of receipt by the IPEA of the translation furnished under Rule 55.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If lack of unity prevents meeting the time limit, the report must be established promptly after receipt of additional fees or after the expiration of the time limit for payment of such fees if no payment is made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention: invitations, restriction or additional fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should consider unity of invention. If lack of unity exists, he may issue an invitation to restrict the claims to a single searched invention or require payment of additional fees under Rule 66.1(e), and may carry out a top-up search or issue a written opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further details on unity and fees are in Chapter 10; in case of non-unity and multiple inventions for which preliminary examination is demanded, examiner may issue invitation then perform top-up search for inventions with fees paid provided they are not excluded under Rule 66.1(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Top-up search practice and scope (Rule 66.1ter)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, the examiner should carry out a top-up search during international preliminary examination to discover relevant documents that became available after the ISR, primarily earlier-filed but later-published patent applications or patents (Rule 64), but also normal prior art and evidence of non-written disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Top-up search scope normally does not extend beyond that of the international search, but final determination is left to the examiner. Top-up searches are normally conducted at the start of examination but may be delayed. No specific search report is established after a top-up search; only particularly relevant newly discovered documents are indicated in the international preliminary examination report (Box V or Box VI as appropriate). The examiner need not carry out a top-up search if it would serve no useful purpose (e.g., subject matter excluded, application too unclear, or no meaningful opinion can be formed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cases where no further written opinion is required
rubrics_metrics.description: If the same Authority acts as both ISA and IPEA and a demand has been filed before the ISA written opinion is prepared, no written opinion is required and the examiner may immediately establish the international preliminary examination report if: (i) the claimed invention satisfies Article 33(1) criteria (novelty, inventive step, industrial applicability); (ii) the application complies with PCT form and contents; (iii) clarity/support requirements met or examiner does not wish to make observations; (iv) no amendment goes beyond the disclosure in the application as filed; (v) all claims relate to an invention in respect of which an ISR is being established and an IPE report is being established for all claims; and (vi) where applicable, sequence listing is available so a meaningful IPE can be carried out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the IPEA does not treat the ISA written opinion as its first written opinion, the same rule applies if criteria (i)–(vi) are satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a further written opinion may be issued
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the applicant has made a credible attempt to overcome or rebut objections in the written opinion but has failed to satisfy the examiner that criteria are met, a further written opinion may, at the IPEA's discretion, be issued if sufficient time remains for establishing the IPE report before expiry of Rule 69.2 time limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the IPEA has carried out a top-up search and intends to raise objections based on prior art discovered in the top-up search, a further written opinion should be issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims for which no international search report has been established
rubrics_metrics.description: International preliminary examination can be carried out only on those inventions in respect of which the ISA has established the ISR. Claims relating to inventions without an ISR need not be the subject of international preliminary examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows from Article 33(6) which requires IPEA to take into consideration documents cited in the ISR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Further stages: additional written opinions and opportunities to amend
rubrics_metrics.description: When the applicant has responded to a written opinion, the examiner may, if necessary and if sufficient time remains, issue one or more additional written opinions. If the applicant requests, the examiner may give one or more additional opportunities to submit amendments or arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional written opinions should invite the applicant to respond and indicate any time limits; time management must consider overall Rule 69.2 report deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nucleotide and/or amino acid sequence listing: compliance and invitations (Annex C)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the international application contains nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences and a corresponding sequence listing complying with the Annex C standard and in an accepted language, the IPEA carries out the international preliminary examination on the basis of the sequence listing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application contains sequences of specified minimum length but no compliant listing or listing not in an accepted language, the IPEA may invite the applicant (Form PCT/IPEA/441) to furnish a compliant listing or translation within a time limit. Furnishing in response to invitation may be subject to a fee not exceeding 25% of the international filing fee (excluding excess sheet fees). If the applicant fails to comply, the IPEA must carry out the examination only to the extent a meaningful examination can be conducted without the sequence listing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority document and translation handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the international application claims priority and the examiner needs the priority document, the examiner should request the International Bureau to furnish a copy. If the priority document is not in a language of the IPEA, the examiner may invite the applicant to furnish a translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the requested priority document or translation has not been timely furnished, the examiner may establish the IPE report as if the priority has not been claimed and indicate this in the report.
